summary: Andrew Howard is CEO and co-founder of Lockchain Corp. (lockchain.ai). Lockchain is an AI-native risk, compliance and monitoring platform for institutions in digital assets, with an exportable audit trail, sourced outputs and a claimed SOC 2 Type II; Howard was previously CEO/CTO of Kudelski Security and led a Georgia Tech UARC. The product matches the fund's auditability thesis, but the company is outside the fund's window and core: it announced a $5M Series A in Feb 2025, filed a further $3M offering in Sept 2026, sells into crypto/digital assets rather than healthcare, insurance or banking, and has a large executive team.

company.name: Lockchain Corp. (Lockchain.ai)
company.what_they_build: AI-native digital-asset intelligence and risk management platform that automates risk, compliance and monitoring workflows for institutions. Features include real-time monitoring across assets, networks, protocols and counterparties, watchlists, custom risk-scoring frameworks, and an exportable institutional audit trail with sourced outputs (S4). A newer tool targets prediction-market contract settlement (S6).
company.customers: Institutions and financial institutions participating in digital assets (S4). Blog content also targets crypto issuers and prediction-market platforms (S6). No named customers; 'Trusted by the biggest names in finance' is unsubstantiated (S4).
company.raised: $5M Series A announced Feb 25, 2025 (S6). Form D filed 2024-12-11: $5,000,000 offered, $4,419,177 sold, 6 investors, first sale 2024-12-02 (S3). Form D filed 2026-09-22: $3,000,000 offered, $1,999,993 sold, 1 investor, first sale 2026-09-08 (S3). An earlier seed round with RSE Ventures participation is mentioned (S7), amount unknown. Backed by Nadia Partners (AI Fund I) LLC (S1).

thesis_fit.belief: Compliance and auditability are the moat in regulated AI, not the model
thesis_fit.evidence: The product is positioned on an exportable institutional audit trail, outputs traceable to their sources ('no black-box conclusions'), SOC 2 Type II, and never training on customer data.

thesis_fit.belief: Founders from inside the industry beat generalists who discover it later
thesis_fit.evidence: Howard comes from cybersecurity and defense R&D (Kudelski Security, Georgia Tech UARC), not from inside financial-institution compliance or digital-asset operations. Co-founder Kehoe has prior risk-management exits.

thesis_fit.belief: Open-source or public traction is the best early signal for technical founders
thesis_fit.evidence: The evidence contains no GitHub, Hacker News, usage metrics or named customers. Public output is limited to blog posts.

thesis_fit.belief: Small teams shipping weekly beat large early rounds
thesis_fit.evidence: The company lists a full C-suite (CEO, CPO, President/CRO, CTO, CSO), a six-person board and six advisors, and has raised roughly $6.4M across two Form D filings. There is no evidence of a weekly shipping cadence.

strengths: Product directly embodies the fund's auditability thesis: logged and exportable assessments, sourced outputs, SOC 2 Type II, no training on customer data (S4).
Experienced security operator as CEO: former CEO/CTO of Kudelski Security and former lead of a Georgia Tech DoD UARC (S5).
Chairman/co-founder Aidan Kehoe has two prior exits in security and risk, to Barracuda and Willis Towers Watson (S5).
Regulation-aware product focus, with content on MiCAR, DORA, SEC issuer filings and ADGM (S6).
Institutional investors and board: White Star Capital and Lerer Hippeau partners on the board; Nadia Partners AI Fund I is a backer (S1, S5).
risks: Stage mismatch: a $5M Series A was announced Feb 2025 (S6) and a further $3M offering was filed in Sept 2026 (S3). Both are beyond the fund's pre-seed/seed focus.

Source conflict on the 2026 round: S1 headlines a '$5.0M round, 6 investors, filed 2026-09-22', but S3 shows that filing is a $3M offering with $1,999,993 sold to 1 investor. The $5M / $4,419,177 / 6-investor figures belong to the 2024-12-11 filing. S2 repeats the same error. Verify directly.
Founding date inconsistency: S1 lists incorporation in 2022, while S7 says co-founded in 2023. S6 ('a year in stealth' before the Apr 2024 launch) fits either.

Website lockchain.ai was guessed from the company name (S4–S6). It appears to be the same company because the footer reads '© 2026 Lockchain Corporation' and Andrew Howard is listed as CEO, but this is not confirmed against the filings.
Sector is crypto/digital-asset compliance, adjacent to rather than within the fund's core of healthcare, insurance and traditional financial services.

Large leadership team, celebrity-heavy board and advisor list (e.g., Anthony Scaramucci), and a co-founder who also runs an investing firm (Matt Higgins / RSE Ventures, S7) suggest a capital-heavy rather than lean team.
Traction is unproven: no named customers, revenue or usage figures, and the 'Trusted by the biggest names in finance' claim is unsupported (S4).
The 2026 offering had $1M of its $3M unsold at filing, with only one investor (S3). This may signal fundraising difficulty or an insider bridge.
S2 is a prior AI-generated screening note, not primary evidence. Its claims were rechecked against S3–S6.
open_questions: Is the Sept 2026 $3M Form D (1 investor, ~$2M sold) a Series A extension, a bridge, or the start of a new priced round, and who is the single investor?
What was the size of the pre-Series A seed round that RSE Ventures joined, and was it raised under a separate filing?
Which institutions currently pay for Lockchain? Can you name any behind 'Trusted by the biggest names in finance', and what is current ARR?
How many people are on the team today, and how often does the product ship? For example, how long did the prediction-market settlement tool take from idea to release?
Who audits the 'every output, sourced' claim? Have any customers' auditors or regulators (e.g., under MiCAR/DORA) reviewed the audit-trail exports?
Do you plan to extend the risk-scoring and audit-trail engine beyond digital assets into traditional banking, insurance or asset-management compliance?
Was Lockchain incorporated in 2022 or founded in 2023, and what happened during the year in stealth before the Apr 2024 launch?
Who on the team brings direct experience from inside a financial institution's risk or compliance function?
conversation_openers: Your Aug 2026 post on prediction-market contract settlement caught my eye. I'd like to hear how the resolution tool uses the same sourced-output and audit-trail approach as the core risk platform.

Your line that '80% of digital asset risk work is data collection, not judgment' matches how we think about compliance software in regulated finance. How do institutions' auditors actually use the exportable assessment logs?

Going from leading a Georgia Tech DoD research center and running Kudelski Security to building custom risk-scoring frameworks for digital-asset institutions is an unusual path. I'd value your view on how the SEC's new crypto issuer filing requirements change what your customers need.
